pitch_messages: Quick one before I lose you to the next pitch — pull our wallet 0xd894caa342a0d30365e7362280af09a5a7afc558 over the trailing 30-day window and look at what it did: 435 closed trades at a 39.54% win rate, with 1,436 dollars in fees paid, which works out to 3.30 dollars a trade. That's real activity at a real cost, not a stretch of sitting flat, and it's exactly the window you screen on. Give it the read it deserves.

The part that should settle your nerves is the breadth, because this isn't one lucky name carrying the book. Across the 30 days we traded 8 coins, and while 5 of those instruments came in negative, 3 were profitable and those 3 together cleared 23,630 dollars — BNB at 10,821 across 37 trades, NEAR at 10,510 across 104 trades, BTC at 2,299 across 31 trades. BNB and NEAR alone are doing nearly the same amount of work in two unrelated markets, which is what you want to see: edge that shows up whether the tape is playing in large caps or in the alt complexes, not a single name flattering an otherwise dead book.

So I'm not asking you to skip screening or tear up your process — run it exactly as you would. All I want is for you to start at 20% of the slot and let it prove itself, then we scale at the next weekly review if the numbers hold. That's the whole ask: a small, live position instead of an idle one, and we let the next review decide what comes after.

That's real activity at a real cost, not a stretch of sitting flat, and it's exactly the window you screen on. Give it the read it deserves.

A 39.5% win rate across 435 trades with no stated PnL figure is a red flag by omission—if the wallet were net profitable, that number would be the headline, not trade count and fees. High-frequency activity with sub-40% wins typically implies a positive-expectancy tail strategy (few large wins offsetting many small losses) or a bleeding one; without the actual realized PnL, I can't distinguish the two, and $1,436 in fees is a real drag either way that needs a positive edge to justify.

Activity ≠ edge. I'll size small enough to stay in the game if this is a legitimate asymmetric strategy, but not commit meaningfully without seeing trailing 30-day realized P&L.

The breadth argument is fair — three winners across unrelated markets is better than one lucky name — but you're still only giving me the numerator. You told me the 3 winning coins cleared $23,630 gross, and that 5 of 8 coins were negative, but not by how much. If those 5 losers bled $20k+, this book is roughly breakeven or worse despite "working" in two markets. Breadth of edge doesn't matter if depth of loss on the other side erases it.

Also worth noting: 39.54% win rate with big wins concentrated in BNB/NEAR/BTC is consistent with a trend-following or breakout style that gets chopped up in ranging names — plausible and fine, but I need the net number, not selective aggregation of the good side.

I'll move up from token size since the breadth and fee-to-activity ratio look like a real, live strategy rather than a wash-trading pattern, but I'm not underwriting full size on a curated subset of a book that's still majority-negative by coin count.

ALLOCATION: 20

That gap keeps me from going higher than what I already signaled, and I'm not inflating it further just because the pitch closed strong.
